title: Two chips, no replacement

feedback.message: That treats the draws as if the first chip went back. Without replacement there is one fewer red and one fewer chip for the second draw.

hints: Use the multiplication rule: P(red first) × P(red second given red first).
P(red first) = [$r]/[$r+b]. How many chips, and how many red ones, are left after that?
solution: $P = \frac{[$r]}{[$r+b]} \times \frac{[$r]-1}{[$r+b]-1}$. After the first red chip is removed there are [$r]−1 red chips among [$r+b]−1 chips.
